A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Motion Attribution for Video Generation and provide complete, readable main text and Appendices A–H. Their equations, tables, figures, and corresponding experiments support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Wan2.1 and Wan2.2 fine-tuning results, a human preference study with 17 participants, attribution ablations, and motion-distribution analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds LTX-2B evaluation and additional Wan2.2 baseline results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same motion-weighted attribution procedure: AllTracker masks, shared timestep and noise, frame-length normalization, projected gradient similarity, and majority-vote selection. Applying the framework to LTX-2B does not introduce a documented algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use VIDGEN-1M and 4DNeX-10M, the same ten motion categories, 50 synthetic query videos, and five evaluation prompts per category. The added LTX-2B evaluation retains this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The Wan2.2 comparison expands from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 1 by adding motion-magnitude selection and V-JEPA. These methods already appeared in the Wan2.1 comparison, but their Wan2.2 participation is new. LTX-2B uses the established comparator suite.

E3.justification: V2 adds an LTX-2B model configuration alongside the retained Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B evaluations. Existing evaluation metrics, selection budgets, query/test construction, training settings, and human-study design remain unchanged; no rerun of retained experiments is established.

E4.justification: V2 Table 5 extends the motion-masking ablation to LTX-2B: dynamic degree is 45.1 with masking versus 41.8 without it. The timestep, projection-dimension, frame-length, motion-distribution, and cross-motion-overlap analyses retain their existing evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting, human preference percentages, and Spearman-correlation analyses retain the same statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: V2 adds a complete LTX-2B comparison: Motive's dynamic degree is 45.1, versus 36.5 for the base model and 38.9 for full fine-tuning. New Wan2.2 rows report dynamic degrees of 44.9 for motion-magnitude selection and 45.6 for V-JEPA. Existing Wan scores and human-study percentages are retained, making this a bounded extension of the reported findings.

T1.justification: The influence formulation, loss construction, projection arguments, and computational-complexity analysis retain their mathematical substance. Equation 13 abbreviates the existing min–max normalization using named extrema; no substantive new assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the claims of scalable motion-specific attribution, frame-length correction, effective selection using 10% of the data, and a 74.1% human preference win rate against the base model. The rewritten conclusion preserves the central contribution and scope.

C2.justification: V2 removes the short main-text limitations paragraph. Its specific warnings about severe occlusion, transparency, and subtle micro-motion are not restored in the appendices. Appendix G.2 retains the limitations concerning computational cost, whole-clip attribution, camera motion, classifier-free guidance, and broader capability tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds Diffusion-Pipe as the implementation source for LTX models. V2 removes the scheduler-index-500 mapping and the final-checkpoint qualifier; timestep 751 remains in Section 4.4. Hardware and runtime disclosures are retained through relocation to Appendix G.1.

R1.justification: V2 adds HaCohen et al.'s LTX-Video reference and Bettencourt et al. on variance reduction with diffusion teachers, including a brief connection in Appendix B.1. The broader related-work discussion and motion-attribution novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 tightens prose throughout the method and experiments, rewrites the conclusion, reorders ablation paragraphs, groups existing future directions, and updates affiliations. The overall section and appendix organization remains recognizable, with localized editorial changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 combines the previously separated Wan evaluations, while Table 5 presents LTX-2B. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 2–3 are compacted, and the projection plot is resized. Figures 4–5 exchange numbering and placement, with additional caption, link-color, and layout refinements.

improvement.justification: The LTX-2B comparison broadens empirical support beyond the Wan family, and the added Wan2.2 baselines strengthen comparative evaluation. These are useful, limited gains with the core findings retained. Removing specific failure conditions and the scheduler-index mapping slightly reduces transparency, but the added evidence supports a modest net improvement.
